summary_html: In Missouri the **juvenile officer**, an officer of the court, takes the case to the judge, not the Children's Division. On written information that a child appears to be within the juvenile court's jurisdiction the juvenile officer makes a preliminary inquiry and may then either make an informal adjustment without a petition or **file a petition** to open a **dependency** (or similar) case (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 211.081.1). Federal funding frameworks (IV-E/ASFA) link court oversight, reasonable-efforts findings, and permanency timelines to downstream actions.
authority_html:
- **ASFA / SSA Title IV-E** — court findings; timelines; permanency planning  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of court/agency performance measures

key_cases.case_name: Greene County Juvenile Office v. K.J.C.
key_cases.holding: The court reversed, holding that the evidence did not clearly and convincingly show the children were without proper care, custody or support, so the juvenile court erred in taking jurisdiction and removing them from an arguably over-protective but not abusive mother.
key_cases.relevance: The decision measures whether the allegations pleaded and proved were sufficient to sustain juvenile-court jurisdiction at all.
key_cases.quote: the trial court must find by clear and convincing evidence that the child is without proper care, custody, or support

key_cases.case_name: Juvenile Officer v. R.O. (In re Z.N.O.)
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the neglect adjudication and change of custody, holding that the circuit court properly confined itself to the allegations pleaded in the petition, that clear and convincing evidence showed the father failed to protect the child from a known abuser, and that a challenge to the specificity of the reasonable-efforts finding was unpreserved absent a Rule 78.07(c) motion.
key_cases.relevance: Z.N.O. holds that the petition's allegations define the scope of the adjudication, which is the core constraint on what a dependency petition can accomplish.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the circuit court did not misapply Section 211.031 by considering evidence solely related to allegations within the petition.

key_cases.holding: The court dismissed the mother's appeal from an adjudication and disposition judgment as moot, because the juvenile court's jurisdiction over the child had ended before the appeal was decided.
key_cases.relevance: J.T.S. shows that challenges to the sufficiency of a dependency petition and the adjudication can be lost to mootness before appellate review occurs.
key_cases.quote: We dismiss the appeal because it is moot.

key_cases.holding: The Court construed Rule 73.01 to mean that the judgment in a court-tried case will be sustained unless there is no substantial evidence to support it, it is against the weight of the evidence, it erroneously declares the law, or it erroneously applies the law, and directed that the labels 'de novo' and 'clearly erroneous' no longer be used.
key_cases.relevance: The same four-part standard governs appellate review of a juvenile-court adjudication entered on a dependency petition, so it is the test any challenge to the sufficiency of that adjudication must meet.
key_cases.quote: The use of the words de novo and clearly erroneous is no longer appropriate in appellate review of cases under Rule 73.01.

timeline_requirements.deadline: 72 hours to complete the standard risk assessment, or the safety assessment tool that replaces it
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Mo. Rev. Stat. § 210.145.

timeline_requirements.deadline: 90 days (120 days for reports involving sexual abuse, or until the investigation is complete in a child fatality or near-fatality case) to notify the alleged perpetrator and the child's parents in writing of the determination
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of the report of abuse or neglect
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: The notification deadline is directory, not mandatory — missing it does not divest the division of authority to continue the investigation or make its determination (annotation to Mo. Rev. Stat. § 210.152, Frye v. Levy, 440 S.W.3d 405 (Mo. banc 2014)).
